title: Transformations of Logarithmic Functions
overview: Stretch it, flip it, slide it: transformations work on logarithmic functions exactly as they do on other functions. By tracking two **anchor points**, $(1, 0)$ and $(10, 1)$, and the vertical asymptote, you can sketch any function of the form $f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$ and find its key features algebraically.
objectives: Describe the roles of $a$, $k$, $d$ and $c$ in $f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$.
Graph transformed logarithmic functions using anchor points and the asymptote.
Factor the argument to identify horizontal translations correctly.
Determine the domain, range, asymptote and intercepts of transformed logarithmic functions.
Write an equation for a transformed logarithmic function from a description or graph.

lessons.title: The parent function and its anchor points
lessons.body:
Every transformed logarithmic function starts from the **parent function** $y = \log x$. Three things are worth memorising about it:

* **Anchor point $(1, 0)$** — because $\log 1 = 0$
* **Anchor point $(10, 1)$** — because $\log 10 = 1$
* **Vertical asymptote $x = 0$** — the graph never touches the $y$-axis

Track these three things through each transformation and you can sketch any logarithmic graph quickly.

```plot
title: The parent function y = log x
f: log(x) | label=y = log x
domain: -1, 12
range: -3, 2
points: (1,0), (10,1), (0.1,-1)
asymptote x: 0
```

The general transformed function is

$$f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$$

| Parameter | Effect | On the anchor point $(x, y)$ |
|---|---|---|
| $a$ | vertical stretch by $\lvert a\rvert$; reflect in $x$-axis if $a < 0$ | $y \to ay$ |
| $k$ | horizontal compression by $\frac{1}{\lvert k\rvert}$; reflect in $y$-axis if $k < 0$ | $x \to \frac{x}{k}$ |
| $d$ | horizontal translation (right if $d > 0$) | $x \to x + d$ |
| $c$ | vertical translation (up if $c > 0$) | $y \to y + c$ |

**Mapping rule:** $(x, y) \to \left(\frac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right)$. The asymptote $x = 0$ moves only with $d$ (it becomes $x = d$).

lessons.title: Translations: y = log(x − d) + c
lessons.body:
**Vertical translation** $y = \log x + c$: every point moves up $c$ units (down if $c < 0$). The asymptote stays at $x = 0$.

**Horizontal translation** $y = \log(x - d)$: every point moves right $d$ units (left if $d < 0$), and so does the asymptote: $x = d$.

> Why the minus sign? $\log(x - 2)$ needs $x = 3$ to get $\log 1 = 0$: the input must be 2 bigger than before, so the graph has moved **right** 2.

**Example:** $y = \log(x - 2) - 5$

```plot
f: log(x) | dashed; label=y = log x
f: log(x-2) - 5 | label=y = log(x − 2) − 5
domain: -1, 14
range: -7, 2
points: (3,-5), (12,-4)
asymptote x: 2
```

* Anchor points: $(1, 0) \to (3, -5)$ and $(10, 1) \to (12, -4)$
* Asymptote: $x = 2$; domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}, x > 2\}$; range $\{y \in \mathbb{R}\}$
* $x$-intercept: $0 = \log(x - 2) - 5 \Rightarrow \log(x - 2) = 5 \Rightarrow x - 2 = 10^5 \Rightarrow x = 100\,002$
* $y$-intercept: $\log(0 - 2) = \log(-2)$ is undefined, so there is none.

lessons.title: Stretches, compressions and reflections
lessons.body:
**Vertical stretch $y = a\log x$.** Multiply every $y$-coordinate by $a$: $(10, 1) \to (10, a)$. $(1, 0)$ doesn't move (0 times anything is 0). If $a < 0$ the graph is also reflected in the $x$-axis — it becomes decreasing.

**Horizontal compression $y = \log(kx)$.** Divide every $x$-coordinate by $k$: for $y = \log(2x)$, $(1, 0) \to (0.5, 0)$ and $(10, 1) \to (5, 1)$. The asymptote stays at $x = 0$.

**Reflection in the $y$-axis $y = \log(-x)$.** The $x$-coordinates change sign: $(1, 0) \to (-1, 0)$. Now the **domain is $x < 0$** — the graph lives on the left of the asymptote.

```plot
title: Reflections of y = log x
f: log(x) | label=y = log x
f: -log(x) | label=y = −log x
f: log(-x) | dashed; label=y = log(−x)
domain: -11, 11
range: -3, 3
points: (1,0), (-1,0)
asymptote x: 0
```

A vertical reflection never changes the domain; a horizontal reflection does.

lessons.title: Combining transformations in the right order
lessons.body:
To graph $f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$:

1. **Make sure it is in this form.** Factor out $k$ if needed: $\log(2x - 4) = \log[2(x - 2)]$. Without factoring you would wrongly translate 4 units instead of 2.
2. **Apply stretches/compressions** ($a$ and $k$).
3. **Apply reflections** (signs of $a$ and $k$).
4. **Apply translations** ($d$ and $c$).

**Example:** $y = \log(-2x) + 4$

| Step | Transformation | $(1, 0)$ | $(10, 1)$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| compress horizontally by $\frac12$ | $y = \log(2x)$ | $(0.5, 0)$ | $(5, 1)$ |
| reflect in $y$-axis | $y = \log(-2x)$ | $(-0.5, 0)$ | $(-5, 1)$ |
| translate up 4 | $y = \log(-2x) + 4$ | $(-0.5, 4)$ | $(-5, 5)$ |

```plot
f: log(-2*x) + 4 | label=y = log(−2x) + 4
domain: -12, 2
range: -2, 7
points: (-0.5,4), (-5,5)
asymptote x: 0
```

Domain $x < 0$, range all reals, asymptote $x = 0$. $x$-intercept: $\log(-2x) = -4 \Rightarrow -2x = 10^{-4} \Rightarrow x = -0.000\,05$.

lessons.title: Finding key features algebraically
lessons.body:
For $f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$ (with $k > 0$):

| Feature | How to find it |
|---|---|
| Vertical asymptote | set the argument equal to 0: $x = d$ |
| Domain | argument $> 0$: $x > d$ (or $x < d$ if $k < 0$) |
| Range | always $\{y \in \mathbb{R}\}$ |
| $x$-intercept | set $f(x) = 0$, isolate the log, rewrite in exponential form |
| $y$-intercept | substitute $x = 0$ — exists only if 0 is in the domain |

**Example:** $y = 5\log(x + 3)$. Asymptote $x = -3$; domain $x > -3$. $x$-intercept: $\log(x + 3) = 0 \Rightarrow x + 3 = 1 \Rightarrow x = -2$. $y$-intercept: $5\log 3 \approx 2.386$.

The same ideas work for other bases, e.g. $y = \log_2(x - 2) + 1$ has asymptote $x = 2$ and passes through $(3, 1)$ and $(4, 2)$.

keyTerms.definition: The basic function $y = \log x$ from which transformed functions are built.
Easy-to-track points on the parent graph, usually $(1, 0)$ and $(10, 1)$ for $y = \log x$.
The line $x = d$ that a logarithmic graph approaches but never crosses; it is where the argument equals 0.
For $y = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$: $(x, y) \to \left(\frac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right)$.
The expression inside the logarithm; it must be positive, which determines the domain.

formulas.name: General transformed logarithmic function
formulas.meaning: $a$: vertical stretch/reflection; $k$: horizontal compression/reflection; $d$: horizontal shift; $c$: vertical shift.

formulas.name: Asymptote and domain
formulas.meaning: Range is always all real numbers.

misconceptions.fact: It moves **right** 3: the input must be 3 larger to give the same output. The asymptote becomes $x = 3$.

misconceptions.myth: $y = \log(2x - 4)$ is a shift of 4 units right.
misconceptions.fact: Factor first: $\log[2(x - 2)]$ is a compression then a shift of **2** right.
Horizontal translations and reflections change the domain, e.g. $y = \log(x + 5)$ has $x > -5$ and $y = \log(-x)$ has $x < 0$.
Only the horizontal translation $d$ moves the vertical asymptote; $a$, $c$ and $k$ do not.

misconceptions.myth: $y = -\log x$ and $y = \log(-x)$ are the same graph.
misconceptions.fact: $-\log x$ is a reflection in the $x$-axis (domain $x > 0$); $\log(-x)$ is a reflection in the $y$-axis (domain $x < 0$).

realWorld.title: Electronics
realWorld.body: Logarithmic amplifiers (op amps) produce an output voltage such as $V_o = 2\log V_i + 5$; the parameters $a$ and $c$ set the gain and offset of the circuit.

realWorld.title: Sound engineering
realWorld.body: Mixing desks use logarithmic sliders: shifting and stretching a log curve changes how volume responds to the slider position.

realWorld.title: Data visualisation
realWorld.body: Scientists translate and stretch log scales so that wide-ranging data (earthquakes, star brightness) fit neatly on a graph.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $y = -\log(x - {{d}}) + {{c}}$: reflect in the $x$-axis, translate right {{d}} and up {{c}}. Anchor points: $(1, 0) \to ({{1+d}}, {{c}})$, $(10, 1) \to ({{10+d}}, {{c-1}})$. Domain $x > {{d}}$; range all reals; asymptote $x = {{d}}$. The graph is decreasing.

(b) $y = {{a}}\log(-x)$: reflect in the $y$-axis and stretch vertically by {{a}}: $(1, 0) \to (-1, 0)$, $(10, 1) \to (-10, {{a}})$. Domain $x < 0$; range all reals; asymptote $x = 0$. As $x$ increases toward 0, $-x$ decreases toward 0, so $\log(-x)$ decreases: the graph is decreasing and falls steeply as it approaches the asymptote.

(c) The reflection in the $x$-axis in (a) did not change the domain, but the reflection in the $y$-axis in (b) changed the domain from $x > 0$ to $x < 0$, because it changes the sign of every $x$-coordinate.

(a) Factor: ${{k}}x - {{m}} = {{k}}\left(x - \frac{ {{m}} }{ {{k}} }\right)$, so $y = \log\left[{{k}}\left(x - {{m/k:3}}\right)\right]$. This is a horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{ {{k}} }$ followed by a translation of {{m/k:3}} units right (not {{m}} units).

questions.text: A student says, "Reflecting a logarithmic function never changes its domain." Evaluate this claim.
questions.modelAnswer:
The claim is only half true.

* A **vertical** reflection $y = -\log x$ multiplies $y$-coordinates by $-1$. The $x$-coordinates are unchanged, so the domain stays $x > 0$ and the range stays all reals.
* A **horizontal** reflection $y = \log(-x)$ multiplies $x$-coordinates by $-1$: $(1, 0) \to (-1, 0)$, $(10, 1) \to (-10, 1)$. The argument $-x$ must be positive, so the domain becomes $x < 0$.

In both cases the range is all real numbers and the asymptote is $x = 0$. Diagram: the vertical reflection flips the graph upside down on the right of the $y$-axis; the horizontal reflection mirrors it onto the left side.

Correct analysis of the horizontal reflection with domain x < 0

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $f$ is $\log x$ compressed vertically by $\frac{1}{ {{n}} }$ and translated {{c}} units down. Anchor points $(1, -{{c}})$ and $(10, {{1/n - c:3}})$; asymptote $x = 0$.

(b) To find $f^{-1}$, swap $x$ and $y$: $x = \frac{1}{ {{n}} }\log y - {{c}}$.

$x + {{c}} = \frac{1}{ {{n}} }\log y \Rightarrow {{n}}(x + {{c}}) = \log y \Rightarrow y = 10^{ {{n}}(x + {{c}}) }$.

(c) $f^{-1}$: domain all reals, range $y > 0$, horizontal asymptote $y = 0$ (the reflection of $x = 0$).

(d) $f^{-1}(-{{c}}+1) = 10^{ {{n}}(1) } = {{10^n}}$. Check: $f({{10^n}}) = \frac{1}{ {{n}} }({{n}}) - {{c}} = {{1 - c}}$ ✓.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $g$ is the reflection of $f$ in the $x$-axis. They are **not** inverses: the inverse of $f$ is $y = 10^x$ (reflection in $y = x$), not a reflection in the $x$-axis.

(b) $h$ is the reflection of $f$ in the $y$-axis. They are not inverses either: $h$ has domain $x < 0$ and $f$'s inverse has domain all reals.

(c) $g$ and $h$ are not inverses. The inverse of $g$: $x = -\log y \Rightarrow y = 10^{-x}$, a decreasing exponential with domain all reals — different from $h$ (domain $x < 0$). In general, two functions are inverses only if one is the reflection of the other in the line $y = x$.

(b) correct relationship and not inverses with reason

(a) Anchor points of $y = \log_2 x$: $(1, 0)$, $(2, 1)$, $(4, 2)$, $(\tfrac12, -1)$. Translate right {{d}} and up {{c}}: $({{1+d}}, {{c}})$, $({{2+d}}, {{c+1}})$, $({{4+d}}, {{c+2}})$.

(b) Asymptote $x = {{d}}$; domain $x > {{d}}$; range all reals.

(c) $x$-intercept: $\log_2(x - {{d}}) = -{{c}} \Rightarrow x - {{d}} = 2^{-{{c}} } \Rightarrow x = {{d + 2^(-c):4}}$.

rubric.point: Correct anchor points for base 2 after translation

questions.text: Explain how each parameter in $f(x) = a\log[k(x - d)] + c$ affects the domain, the range and the vertical asymptote of the graph.
questions.modelAnswer:
* $a$ (vertical stretch/reflection): changes only $y$-coordinates — no effect on the domain, range (still all reals) or asymptote.
* $k$ (horizontal compression/stretch): scales $x$-coordinates toward or away from $x = d$; if $k > 0$ the domain stays on the same side; if $k < 0$ (reflection in the $y$-axis) the domain switches to $x < d$. Asymptote unchanged.
* $d$ (horizontal translation): moves the asymptote to $x = d$ and the domain to $x > d$ (or $x < d$).
* $c$ (vertical translation): moves every point up or down; no effect on domain, range or asymptote.

The range of every transformed logarithmic function is $\{y \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

rubric.point: Correct effect of k including reflection
Correct effect of d on asymptote/domain
Correct effect of c and statement that range is always all reals

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the $y$-intercept.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Factor the argument: $-\frac12 x + {{m}} = -\frac12(x - {{2*m}})$. So $f(x) = -\frac12\log\left[-\frac12(x - {{2*m}})\right] + 2$.

Transformations: vertical compression by $\frac12$ and reflection in the $x$-axis ($a = -\frac12$); horizontal stretch by a factor of 2 and reflection in the $y$-axis ($k = -\frac12$); translation {{2*m}} units right and 2 units up.

(b) Argument $> 0$: $-\frac12(x - {{2*m}}) > 0 \Rightarrow x < {{2*m}}$. Domain $x < {{2*m}}$; range all reals; asymptote $x = {{2*m}}$.

(c) $x$-intercept: $\log\left(-\frac12 x + {{m}}\right) = 4 \Rightarrow -\frac12 x + {{m}} = 10^4 \Rightarrow x = 2({{m}} - 10\,000) = {{2*(m - 10000)}}$.

(d) $y$-intercept: $f(0) = -\frac12\log {{m}} + 2 \approx {{-0.5*log(m) + 2:4}}$.

questions.text: Create a logarithmic function that includes **all** of the following transformations of $y = \log x$: a horizontal stretch, a translation to the left, a vertical translation, and a reflection.
questions.modelAnswer:
Sample answer: $y = -\log\left[\frac12(x + 3)\right] + 2$.

* $k = \frac12$: horizontal stretch by a factor of 2
* $d = -3$: translation 3 units left
* $c = 2$: translation 2 units up
* $a = -1$: reflection in the $x$-axis

Anchor points: $(1, 0) \to (2 - 3, 2) = (-1, 2)$; $(10, 1) \to (20 - 3, -1 + 2) = (17, 1)$.

Domain $x > -3$; range all reals; asymptote $x = -3$.

(Any function with $0 < |k| < 1$, $d < 0$, $c \neq 0$ and $a < 0$ or $k < 0$ is acceptable, with consistent key features.)

rubric.point: Includes a translation left and a vertical translation
Correct domain, range and asymptote for their function
